## Purpose
Provide a precise, always-current progress surface for the project using exactly four status levels:
- `Done`
- `Mostly Done`
- `In Progress`
- `Not Started`

This file is the authoritative live tracking view for "where we are now".

## Status Rules
- `Done`: the tracked claim is backed by a formally exhaustive, machine-checkable proof surface with no plausible coverage gap remaining for that claim.
- `Mostly Done`: the core implementation is landed and validated with strong executable evidence, but closure still depends on bounded follow-up work such as auto-derived exhaustiveness, stronger coverage proof, or removal of curated/manual proof gaps.
- `In Progress`: meaningful implementation has started, but core capabilities or validation are still missing.
- `Not Started`: no meaningful implementation has landed yet.

## Update Policy
- Review and update this file before every commit when a task changes actual project closure, remaining scope, or the next most important gap.
- When any live-status row changes, log that change here before commit and explicitly surface the changed snapshot in the user-facing completion message for that task.
- Even when no row changes, the commit-workflow completion message must still display the current live-status snapshot so task impact on the tracker stays visible.
- When a task does not change live status, say that status is unchanged rather than implying drift.
- Use only the four statuses above.
- Keep "Evidence" concrete and "Left To Close" explicit.
- Do not mark a row `Done` if its proof surface still depends on a curated/manual construct list where grammar-derived exhaustiveness is expected.
- Universal parser doctrine: any PGEN EBNF-based parser family is judged against the same professional-grade closure bar. Status differences across parser families reflect different amounts of landed proof, not different quality standards.

Tracker note (2026-06-07): **NEW TREE `EBNF-SOURCE-OF-TRUTH` (`PGEN-EBNF-SOT-0001`, `.1` DONE) — root-caused how a grammar-driven generator can emit parser-rejected output, and named the binding rule LOUD.** The director correctly flagged the regex-6 finding as fishy (it should be impossible for an EBNF-derived generator to produce EBNF-parser-rejected strings). TOOL-BACKED root cause (`parseability_probe`): `regex.ebnf` STRUCTURALLY accepts `\u{…}` (`unicode_escape`) and `(*<any-name>)` (`directive_verb`), so the generator emits them — but a SEPARATE hand-written validator, `rust/src/regex_compile_validation.rs` (referenced by neither the generator nor the EBNF), rejects `\u` and unrecognized `(*verb)` names. So the regex parser's accepted language = (structural EBNF) ∩ (out-of-band validator), the generator targets only the EBNF, and the difference is the generated-but-rejected set. **THE RULE: the EBNF (+ its `@predicate`/`@generate`/`@semantic` annotations) is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the accepted language; an out-of-band acceptance validator the generator cannot see is a DEFECT** — encode it in the EBNF (semantic annotation) or remove/relax it. Recorded loud in the book (`quality-and-closure-model.md`), a KM card (`ebnf-single-source-of-truth`), a decision record, and this new tree; plus a standing discipline (`feedback_be_alert_root_cause_fishy_immediately`). Also corrected the G.4.9 over-claim (`(?|)`/`(?P>)`/`(?(…))` parse; only `\u`/`(*verb)` fail). Docs-only; status unchanged across all parser-family rows.

Tracker note (2026-05-26): **`SV-EXH-PROOF.3.3.4.b.6.2.37.7` DONE — SV GRAMMAR FIX: `expression_or_cond_pattern` gains `inside_expression` sibling so `if (x inside {…})` parses; uvm_pkg furthest 1,278,335 → 1,508,106; release 1.0.130 → 1.0.131, schema STAYS 3 (`PGEN-SV-EXH-PROOF-0094`).** One-rule grammar edit at `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf:2018`. Surfaced by `.37.6`'s 1,278,335 furthest reaching `uvm_root::die`'s `if (get_core_state() inside {UVM_CORE_PRE_ABORT, UVM_CORE_ABORTED})`. The `cond_predicate` rule used by `if`/`while`/`for` conditions had `expression_or_cond_pattern := expression_base | cond_pattern` — bypassing `expression`'s outer alternation `expression := expression_base | inside_expression`. Tracker note (2026-05-25): **`SV-EXH-PROOF.3.3.4.b.6.2.36.3` DONE — investigation using `.36.2`'s tool pinned the TRUE ROOT CAUSE: memoization caches parse results but NOT semantic-runtime side effects (`PGEN-SV-EXH-PROOF-0084`).** Bundled instrumentation extension (codegen-level fast-path now also pushes/pops the rule_context_stack, closing a chain-trace gap in `.36.2`). Tracker note (2026-05-21): **`SV-EXH-PROOF.3.3.4.b.3` DONE — PARSER-AGNOSTIC ENGINE LAYER 0: unified quantifier engine; uniform per-iteration atomicity across `?` / `*` / `+` / `{N}` / `{N,M}` / `{N,}` / `{,M}`; release 1.0.126 (schema stays 3); SV external corpus stays 8/14 — Layer 0 is INFRASTRUCTURE; regex broader corpus / RGX conformance ✅ 44/0 unaffected (proves the unified codegen is behavior-equivalent across the entire conformance suite) (`PGEN-SV-EXH-PROOF-0029`).** User strategic line (2026-05-21): "After Layer 0, all the repetition in the EBNF shall have the right behavior." Prior codegen in `rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs::generate_quantified_logic` (and `ast_code_generator.rs::generate_quantified_content`) special-cased exactly three operators (`*`, `+`, `?`) in three independently-written code paths, with an asymmetric defect — the FIRST iteration of `+` was emitted INLINE without `try_parse` wrapping. Bounded forms (`{N}` / `{N,M}` / `{N,}` / `{,M}`) declared in `grammars/ebnf.ebnf:149-189` were never implemented (the `_ => Err("Unknown quantifier")` fallthrough). **Fix:** new `parse_quantifier_bounds(quantifier: &str) -> Option<(usize, Option<usize>)>` helper in `rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs` maps every surface form to `(min, max)` (4 unit tests cover happy path + whitespace + invalid forms incl. `{5,2}` rejected). Both codegen functions rewritten as ONE `loop` with EVERY iteration wrapped in `try_parse` (per-iteration atomicity is uniform). When `min > 0`, codegen emits `let quantifier_start_position = parser.position;` before the loop and restores `parser.position = quantifier_start_position;` on min-failure before `Err(Backtrack)` — quantifier-level atomicity (the user's stated `{N}` semantics: "the cursor is left at the position it had before trying to match `<group>{N}`"). For `min == 0` (`*` / `?`) the bind + check are elided to avoid always-false comparisons + 495 unused-variable warnings. Max-count (`{N}` / `{N,M}` / `{,M}`) emits `if iteration_count >= #m_lit { break; }`. Zero-length guard + SAFETY_LIMIT (10_000) preserved. **Release bump, NO schema bump** — `?` / `*` / `+` BEHAVIOR-EQUIVALENT on success; BEHAVIOR-EQUIVALENT-OR-MORE-CORRECT on failure (prior `+` first-iter inline path could leak partial cursor; unified path rolls back at the quantifier boundary). Bounded forms unparseable pre-fix; Layer 0 makes them parser-agnostic infrastructure (no current grammar uses them); SVPP-0002/REGEX-0083 strictly-more-permissive category. USER SEMANTICS, CONFIRMED IMPLEMENTED: per-iter cursor save+restore (handled by `try_parse`) + quantifier-level atomicity for `min > 0` (handled by `quantifier_start_position`). VERIFIED: lib **465/465** PASS no-features (+4 `parse_quantifier_bounds` unit tests); SV smoke (`module m; endmodule` / `if (1) $display("ok");` / else-if chain / for-loop) PASS via fresh release `parseability_probe`; SV shape-contract GREEN. **RGX broader corpus / conformance 44/0 ✅** via `cargo run --features generated_parsers --release --bin test_runner -- --parser regex` after `make focus_regex` regen — proves the unified codegen produces a regex parser with identical behavior across the entire conformance suite. **SV external corpus `8/14 → 10/14`** (fresh triage gate 2026-05-21 09:55) — `friscv_rv32i_core ×{2017,2023}` now PASS. HONEST ROOT-CAUSE UPDATE: I had hypothesised Layer 0 was pure infrastructure with no corpus delta expected; the gate proved that wrong by +2 cases. The friscv_rv32i blocker was NOT a separate statement-level grammar defect (the prior `.3.3.6` categorization); it was the prior codegen's asymmetric `+`-first-iter-not-wrapped-in-`try_parse` defect. Layer 0 wraps the first iter of `+` uniformly with every other iter — the cursor rolls back cleanly on first-iter failure — and friscv_rv32i parses end-to-end. The BEHAVIORAL DIFFERENCE on the prior `+` first-iter-FAILURE path was real (not behavior-equivalent as I had claimed at design time). Residual 4 fails: uvm_pkg/uvm_compat_pkg ×{2017,2023} STILL fail (uvm_pkg_2017 at IDENTICAL byte 113637 vs .b.1 — Layer 0 preserves uvm behavior; blocked by the next LRM-extraction-defect class). `.3.3.6` task entry can be CLOSED — friscv_rv32i is PASS without needing a separate grammar fix. Tracker note (2026-05-20): **`SV-EXH-PROOF.3.3.3` DONE — FIRST DELIBERATE ENGINE FIX (parser-agnostic, in the generator) + SV grammar wrapper composite; classic Rust `?`-bypasses-cleanup bug in `with_semantic_runtime_rule_transaction` (SEMTRACE-pinned after 3 prior hypotheses disproven); release 1.0.121, AST-dump schema stays `3`; minimal repro `my_t [3:0] x` PASSES (was unfixable); regex broader corpus / RGX conformance ✅ 44/0 unaffected; external-corpus stays `6/14` (foundation engine fix — `.3.3.4` cross-package import is the corpus mover) (`PGEN-SV-EXH-PROOF-0024`).** Root cause (SEMTRACE-definitive across 1664 trace lines): `with_semantic_runtime_rule_transaction` (`rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs`) `std::mem::take`-s `self.semantic_runtime_state` (leaving `Default==new()` valid-but-EMPTY), then performs `?`-fallible calls (`f(self)?`, `apply_*?`, `resolve_predicate?`); a `?` early-return propagated out of the ENTIRE function, JUMPING OVER the trailing `if result.is_err() { restore original }` — leaving self.state EMPTY, silently destroying every fact emitted by prior COMMITTED sibling rules. Decisive evidence: `RESTORE` fired **0×** / `took post-body state (self.state→EMPTY)` **9×** / fact-flow `declared_type_identifier facts(1)=[type_name=my_t] EXIT OK → … → use-site facts(0)=[] never restored`. **Fix (engine, parser-agnostic, IIFE/"try-block" emulation)**: wrap the fallible body in `(|| -> ParseResult<…> {…})()` so every `?` returns into `result`, making the restore reachable on every non-commit exit. Zero `unsafe`; zero behaviour change on success; benefits every generated parser. RAII Drop-guard considered (panic-safe by strict def.) but rejected: not cleanly safe-Rust here (post-take body calls `&self` methods, guard would conflict; only `*mut`+`unsafe` works); deferred since `Default==new()` makes IIFE panic-ROBUST (parser never `catch_unwind`s mid-parse). **Fix (SV grammar composite)**: `checked_type_identifier := type_identifier -> {body:$1.body}` + `@predicate has_fact args:[type_name,$body]`, routing `known_unscoped_block/data_type_identifier` through it (proven `.3.3.1`/`.3.3.2` idiom). **Release bump 1.0.120→1.0.121, schema STAYS 3** (strictly-more-permissive; affected declarations were silently unparseable, no such AST ever emitted; SVPP-0002/REGEX-0083 category). VERIFIED: minimal repro PASSES; SEMTRACE confirmed RESTORE fires 110× (was 0); use-site `has_fact[type_name,my_t]` resolves+TRUE; class/typedef/let/`#(parameter…)`/localparam/builtin-dim no-regression (memo ON, normal). Inventory **2297→2299** (+2: new wrapper). SV shape-contract GREEN. **regex broader corpus / RGX conformance ✅ 44/0** (critical downstream unaffected). external-corpus **stays `6/14`** — `.3.3.3` is the FOUNDATION engine fix (the `?`-bypass state-leak was masking every downstream semantic-fact-based fix); residual 8 cases blocked by DISTINCT defects → **`.3.3.4` cross-package `import pkg::*` type-name visibility (the actual corpus mover, ~6 cases — veer ×2 + uvm ×2 + uvm_compat ×2)** + `.3.3.6` (statement-level, friscv_rv32i ×2). Pre-existing `auto_gate_regex/rtl_const_expr_inventory_wide_shape` failures (decisively confirmed pre-existing at `.3.3.2` via git-stash baseline check) tracked as `.3.3.5`. Strategic line (user 2026-05-20): EBNF + the AST-pipeline engine must acquire all the parser-agnostic features needed to cleanly and elegantly parse the whole external SV corpus; `.3.3.3` IIFE is the first such parser-agnostic engine feature; `.3.3.4` will follow the same lens. Tracker note (2026-05-03): **regex.ebnf slice 40 of N — `modifier_item` per-branch typed (closes `inline_modifiers.spec` end-to-end).** Twelfth sub-rule typing slice. modifier_item split from 3 branches with internal optionals into 5 explicit branches: `"a" restrict -> {char:"a", restrict:$2}` / `"a" -> "a"` / `"xx" -> "xx"` / `"x" -> "x"` / `modifier_char` passthrough. Eliminates the `[]` interleaving from slice 39's set/unset arrays. Empirical: `(?ix)` → `set:["i", "x"]` (was `["i", "x", []]`); `(?aDx)` → `set:[{char:"a", restrict:"D"}, "x"]` (mixed string + object); `(?xx)` → `set:["xx"]` (matched doubled-x branch). **`inline_modifiers.spec` and `scoped_inline_modifiers.spec` now end-to-end typed across 4 sub-rule levels** (slices 24+31+39+40). A complete `(?aDx-m)` surfaces as `{type:"atom", kind:"inline_modifiers", spec:{reset:false, seq:{set:[{char:"a", restrict:"D"}, "x"], unset:["m"]}}}`. **Contract bump:** parser release `1.1.69` → `1.1.70`; contract `1.1.71` → `1.1.72`. New "Release 1.1.70 / Contract 1.1.72" section in [docs/contracts/PGEN_REGEX_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md](docs/contracts/PGEN_REGEX_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md). Tracker note (2026-05-03): **regex.ebnf slice 39 of N — `modifier_seq` + `modifier_group` typed (`{set, unset}` shape).** Eleventh sub-rule typing slice. 4 grammar changes: modifier_seq split from 2 branches (with parens-grouped optional pair) into 3 explicit branches; modifier_group `[$1**]` flatten-spread. Same parens-grouped-optional-pair workaround pattern as slice 37 (version_number) — split into N explicit branches. Set/unset arrays may have interleaved `[]` markers for optional-sub-element items (e.g. `(?ix)` → `set:["i", "x", []]` where the trailing `[]` is the un-matched `"x"?` slot inside the `"x" "x"?` modifier_item branch). Tracker note (2026-05-03): **regex.ebnf slice 38 of N — `returned_capture_subroutine` outer typed.** Tenth sub-rule typing slice. 1 annotation: `returned_capture_subroutine -> {subroutine:$1, captures:$2}`. Empirical: `(?&name(1))` → `target:{subroutine:{kind:"named", name:"name"}, captures:["(", {sign:[], value:1}, [], ")"]}`. **Field-naming decision:** inner field is `subroutine` (not `target`) to avoid `target.target.kind` collision with the outer `subroutine_call.target`. Tracker note (2026-05-02): **regex.ebnf slice 18 of N — `quoted_literal` typed.** First atom-subtree slice after the escape closure. `quoted_literal = "\\Q" quoted_literal_char* "\\E" -> {type:"atom", kind:"quoted_literal", body:$2}`. Empirical: `\Qhello\E` → `{type:"atom", kind:"quoted_literal", body:["h","e","l","l","o"]}` (was `["\\Q", [<chars>], "\\E"]`); `\Q\E` → `{body:[]}`; `\Qabc def\E` → `{body:["a","b","c"," ","d","e","f"]}`. `body` is the array of `quoted_literal_char*` matches — single-char strings, with `quoted_literal_escaped_char` producing 2-char strings that preserve the `\` and the escaped char. Consumers join the array for the literal string (`body.join("")`); semantic-aware consumers can distinguish escaped vs raw chars from element shapes. Routes through `quoted_literal`: only the atom-fallback cases of the `\Q...\E quantifier?` family table (no trailing quantifier OR single-char body OR empty body with quantifier) — the multi-piece family-table fast path goes through `piece_quoted_run_quantified` which does NOT touch `quoted_literal`, so PGEN-RGX-0074/0077 family-table cases are unchanged. Picked `quoted_literal` over leaf-char atoms (literal/dot/whitespace_literal) because typing leaf chars inflates AST size 4× for the most common case; `quoted_literal` is lower volume and higher value. **Contract bump:** parser release `1.1.47` → `1.1.48`; contract `1.1.49` → `1.1.50`. Tracker note (2026-05-01): **PGEN-RGX-0077 closed** — `[$1**]` flatten-spread peels `Alternative`. RGX bug report: every multi-char `\Q...\E quantifier?` source produced one extra wrapping layer at `pattern[0][0]` (`[[<N pieces>]]` instead of the documented flat `[<N pieces>]`). Adjacent regression to PGEN-RGX-0075 on a different codegen path. Root cause: the `[$1**]` flatten-spread codegen in [rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_return_transform.rs](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_return_transform.rs) did not peel `Alternative` wrapping before inspecting child content for the unwrap decision; the codegen wraps Or-rule and rule-reference branch results in `Alternative(boxed_inner)`, so for `concatenation = piece+ -> [$1**]` each piece node arrives as `Alternative(piece_inner_node)` — pre-fix the inner match saw `Alternative` and fell into the "push as-is" arm. Fix: peel `Alternative` recursively before unwrap decision, plus preventative `Json(Value::Array(_))` arm. Empirical: `\Qab*\E{2,}` → 3 pieces flat (was wrapped); `\Qabcdef\E+` → 6 pieces flat; degenerate `\Qa\E{3}` and `\Q\E{2}` unaffected (atom-fallback path); plain literal `abc`/`hello` unaffected. New regression-lock test `regex_parser_pgen_rgx_0077_quoted_run_quantified_pieces_flat_in_concatenation` pins family-table (9 shapes from bug report) — asserts piece count + atom values + quantifier-on-last-piece + no-quantifier-on-inner-pieces. **Contract bump:** parser release `1.1.39` → `1.1.40`; contract `1.1.41` → `1.1.42`. Tracker note (2026-05-01): **PGEN-RGX-0076 closed** — typed `posix_class` shape. RGX bug report `/Users/richarddje/Documents/github/rgx/pgen-issues/PGEN-RGX-0076.yaml` showed that every POSIX class inside `[...]` collapsed to the literal string `"[:"` because the `posix_class` rule used a placeholder annotation `-> $1` that extracted only the opening delimiter. The book chapter `rules-char-class.md` already acknowledged this as a known sub-optimal annotation. Fix: `posix_class -> {type:"posix_class", name:$3, negated:$2}` and `posix_negation -> true`. Surfaced two latent codegen bugs in [rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_return_transform.rs](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_return_transform.rs): `BooleanLiteral` and `NumberLiteral` rule-level scalar paths were emitting `ParseContent::Terminal(<stringified>)` instead of typed `Json(Bool/Number)` — surfaced when `posix_negation -> true` produced the string `"true"` rather than the boolean. Both codegen sites fixed to mirror the value-extraction path. Empirical: `[[:alpha:]]` → `{"type":"posix_class","name":"alpha","negated":[]}`; `[[:^alpha:]]` → `{"type":"posix_class","name":"alpha","negated":true}`; `[[:alpha:][:digit:]]` → 2-element class_body with both POSIX classes typed and disambiguated. `negated` convention: `true` (matched `^`) or `[]` (un-matched `posix_negation?` slot — consumers map `[]` → `false`); same convention as `quantifier.greediness`. **Contract bump:** parser release `1.1.36` → `1.1.37`; contract `1.1.38` → `1.1.39`. Tracker note (2026-05-01): **regex.ebnf slice 6 of N — quantifier-subtree typed-shape campaign CLOSED.** Final two grammar changes consolidate the subtree: (1) `quant_base` reshaped from per-branch `-> $1` (heterogeneous string/object output) to per-branch typed `{min, max}` for every alternative — shorthand quantifiers expand to PCRE2-equivalent bounds (`*` → `{0,null}`, `+` → `{1,null}`, `?` → `{0,1}`); counted-quantifier branch passes through via `$1`. (2) `quantifier` rule annotated `-> {type:"quantifier", min:$1.min, max:$1.max, greediness:$2}` — emits a fully typed `{type, min, max, greediness}` object directly. Consumer-visible AST shape change for the `quantifier` field on each piece: was a `[<base>, <suffix>]` 2-tuple, now a typed object (or `[]` for un-quantified pieces, unchanged). Empirical: `a*` → `{"type":"quantifier","min":0,"max":null,"greediness":[]}`; `a{2,5}+` → `{"type":"quantifier","min":2,"max":5,"greediness":"possessive"}`; pieces with no quantifier still emit `[]`. Greediness convention: `"lazy"`/`"possessive"` for matched suffixes, `[]` for un-matched (consumers map `[]` → `"greedy"` until a future slice adds an annotation-language coalesce operator). All six rules in the quantifier subtree are now annotated (`digits` typed integer, `quant_suffix` typed enum, `counted_quantifier_body` typed `{min, max}`, `counted_quantifier` `-> $3` passthrough, `quant_base` typed `{min, max}` per branch, `quantifier` typed `{type, min, max, greediness}`). Tracker note (2026-05-01): **PGEN-RGX-0075 closed** — typed-shape correctness for multi-piece concatenation. RGX bug report `/Users/richarddje/Documents/github/rgx/pgen-issues/PGEN-RGX-0075.yaml` showed that `concatenation = piece+ -> [$1**]` was producing only the first piece for plain inputs like `"abc"` — `"b"` and `"c"` were silently dropped from the typed AST array (RGX's lib suite collapsed to ~73% pass rate purely from this). Root cause: `$N` PositionalRef codegen in [rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_return_transform.rs](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_return_transform.rs) peeled `elements[0].content.clone()` from a `Quantified` base when `captured_vars.len() == 1`, treating Quantified-bodied rules like single-element Sequence wrappers — violating the platform-book annotation-system policy that says `$1` on a Quantified body is "the whole capture group". Why the `\Q...\E` test corpus didn't catch it: `\Qab*\E{2,}` and similar produce 3 pieces correctly because `piece+` matches a SINGLE piece whose content is itself a Sequence-of-3 from `piece_quoted_run_quantified`'s annotation; the bug only surfaced on plain multi-piece concatenations that no test exercised. Fix in three codegen sites (`generate_positional_ref`, `generate_value_extraction`, `generate_quantified_extraction`): remove the Quantified peel-arm so Quantified bases fall through to `other.clone()`. Compensating grammar change: `regex = pattern -> {...}` (was `regex = pattern? -> {...}`) — the pre-fix `?` propped up the buggy auto-peel; the inner `alternative = concatenation?` already handles emptiness, so the outer `?` was redundant. New regression-lock test `regex_parser_pgen_rgx_0075_multi_piece_concatenation_surfaces_all_pieces` in [rust/src/embedding_api.rs](rust/src/embedding_api.rs) pins empirical shape for `"a"`/`"ab"`/`"abc"`/`"hello"` (asserts piece count and atom values). `cargo test --lib --features generated_parsers --features ebnf_dual_run` 494 / 0 (was 493 + the new test). Empirical probe sweep confirms all of `"a"`/`"ab"`/`"abc"`/`"hello"`/`"a*"`/`"[a-z]"`/`"a|b"`/`"(abc)"`/`"\\d+"`/`"foo\\Kbar"`/`""` produce correct typed shapes with span matching input length. **Contract bump:** parser release `1.1.34` / contract `1.1.36`. New section in [docs/contracts/PGEN_REGEX_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md](docs/contracts/PGEN_REGEX_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md); new `REGEX-0075` entry in [docs/contracts/PGEN_RELEASED_PARSER_BUG_LEDGER.md](docs/contracts/PGEN_RELEASED_PARSER_BUG_LEDGER.md). Regex AST schema version stays `1`. Live-docs sync: regex parser book chapters [changelog-index.md (new 1.1.34 entry), schema-versioning.md (0.9.0 row), rules-top-level.md (regex = pattern, history note)] — `make regex_parser_book_gate` green. Status stays unchanged across all parser-family rows. RGX integration impact: consumers walking `regex.pattern[0][0]` now see every piece; RGX should bump PGEN pin and re-run their lib suite, expected recovery from 73% to baseline.

Tracker note (2026-05-01): Task #38 closed — parens-grouped-Or trailing-annotation broadcast. Codegen now correctly applies a trailing return annotation on a parens-grouped Or to every alternative inside the group, not just the first. Two extractors fixed in lockstep: `extract_rule_annotations` in [rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs](rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs) and the cross-checker `extract_declared_annotations_from_json` in [rust/src/ast_shape_contract.rs](rust/src/ast_shape_contract.rs). Both now track a `group_open_branch_stack` and remember `last_closed_group_range` at each `)`; on the immediately-following `return_*`, broadcast the annotation to that range. The disambiguation cases all behave per the principle "the trailing annotation applies to the alternatives inside the just-closed group ONLY when it directly follows the group's close" (covered: `(A|B)->ann` broadcasts; `A|B->ann` is per-branch; `A|(B|C)->ann` broadcasts to B and C only; nested groups; etc.). Empirical proof: `parseability_probe --parse-dump-ast-pretty return_annotation "'hello'"` was producing raw `Sequence` (single-quoted branch fell through to raw passthrough); now produces `Json({"type":"string","value":"hello"})` matching the double-quoted branch. Subsequent grammar refactor: `quant_base` in [grammars/regex.ebnf](grammars/regex.ebnf) flipped from slice-5's per-branch workaround `"*" -> $1 | "+" -> $1 | ...` to the factored form `( "*" | "+" | "?" | counted_quantifier ) -> $1` — semantically identical, more elegant, demonstrates the fix end-to-end. `cargo test --lib --features generated_parsers --features ebnf_dual_run` 493 / 0. Manifest `rust/test_data/ast_shape_contract/return_annotation_v1.json` updated with new branch=1 entry for `string_literal`. `make regex_parser_book_gate` green. Live-docs sync: regex parser book chapters [rules-quantifier.md, changelog-index.md, schema-versioning.md] reflect the factored form and the #38 fix; platform mdBook [docs/book/src/annotation-system.md](docs/book/src/annotation-system.md) gains a new "Parens-grouped Or with trailing annotation — broadcast" section adjacent to the existing "Implicit `-> $1` default" section. No contract identity bump (regex grammar shape unchanged; return_annotation grammar shape change was a buggy → correct fix not in a versioned consumer chain). Status stays unchanged across all parser-family rows. Task #38 moves from `pending` to `completed`. Task #40 ("Annotate regex.ebnf for full AST usability") remains in-progress; remaining quantifier-subtree slice: `quantifier`. Then atom subtree, class subtree, etc.

Tracker note (2026-05-01): Standalone regex parser mdBook landed at [docs/regex_parser_book/](docs/regex_parser_book/) — the canonical AST integration reference for downstream consumers (RGX in particular). 24 chapters covering: cold-clone build recipe, public API surface, AST envelope structure, all six `ParseContent` variants and the `Json` carrier, walking patterns, per-rule shape reference (top-level, piece + quoted-run family, quantifier subtree, atom 25-way Or with discriminator table, character class, group family, modifier subtree, escape subtree, anchors/backrefs/misc), worked examples for every regex feature (literals, quantifiers across all 7 PCRE2 forms × 3 greediness modes, char classes, groups + alternation, the `\Q...\E` family table, anchors with discriminator function, escapes with classification function), migration from the pre-1.1.30 recursive envelope, schema-versioning policy, glossary, and a release-by-release changelog index. **The book is deliberately aligned with the parser state at commit `6e5b0f23`** (PGEN-RGX-0074 fix + slices 1-2 of typed-shape work, parser release `1.1.33` / contract `1.1.35`) so RGX can pin to that PGEN tag/commit and read a book that exactly describes the AST it observes; alignment-forward to the post-slice-3+4 state will land in a follow-up commit. RGX consumes the book via the PGEN submodule — either reads the `.md` source files at `<pgen-checkout>/docs/regex_parser_book/src/*.md` directly off disk, or browses the rendered HTML at `<pgen-checkout>/docs/regex_parser_book-html/index.html` (also accessible via github.com web UI). No build step required on the RGX side. Build path: `make regex_parser_book_gate` (uses `mdbook build docs/regex_parser_book` and writes HTML to sibling `docs/regex_parser_book-html/`). **Both source markdown AND rendered HTML are TRACKED in git** so the book is browsable directly on GitHub without requiring mdbook installation — diverges from the platform book's `docs/book-html/` gitignored convention specifically because RGX integration needs github.com browsability. Gate script `rust/scripts/regex_parser_book_gate.sh` checks the chapter set and asserts the build passes. Integration contract document now has a `## Companion Documentation` section pointing to the book. No parser code changes; no contract identity bump. Status stays unchanged across all parser-family rows. Task #45 ("Create regex parser mdBook for RGX as canonical AST reference") moves to `Done`. Task #40 ("Annotate regex.ebnf for full AST usability") remains in-progress.

Tracker note (2026-04-30): regex.ebnf annotation work — slice 3 of N (`counted_quantifier_body` typed `{min, max}` shape) + new `null` literal primitive in the return-annotation language. The original 2-branch rule was restructured into 4 explicit branches per logical case (`{n,m}`, `{n,}`, `{n}`, `{,m}`); each branch has its own per-branch annotation producing `{min: <int>, max: <int|null>}`. The `null` literal is JSON's sixth value type — added to the return-annotation language alongside object/array/string/number/boolean (`UnifiedReturnAST::NullLiteral`, codegen lowers to `serde_json::Value::Null`, grammar surface `null_literal := 'null' -> {type: "null"}`). Also fixed a related papercut: `NumberLiteral` codegen now preserves integer typing when the literal has no fractional part, so `{min: 0, ...}` produces `"min": 0` instead of `"min": 0.0`. Empirical: `a{2,5}` → `{"min":2,"max":5}`; `a{2,}` → `{"min":2,"max":null}`; `a{2}` → `{"min":2,"max":2}`; `a{,5}` → `{"min":0,"max":5}`. `cargo test --lib --features generated_parsers --features ebnf_dual_run` 493 passed. No contract bump on this commit — bump and ledger entry land on the slice that closes the quantifier subtree (`quant_base` and `quantifier` rules). Status stays unchanged across all parser-family rows. Then atom subtree, class subtree, etc.

Tracker note (2026-04-30): PGEN-RGX-0074 closed — `\Q...\E` quantifier-attachment correctness. Two parser-agnostic changes landed together. (1) New `**` flatten-spread primitive in the return-annotation language (`UnifiedReturnAST::FlattenSpread { base }`, codegen in [rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_return_transform.rs](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_return_transform.rs)::generate_array_transform, grammar surface in [grammars/return_annotation.ebnf](grammars/return_annotation.ebnf), typed-tree reader recognizes `{type:"flat_spread", base:...}`). Like single-`*` spread, but for each pushed child whose content is Sequence/Quantified, unwraps one level — lets a child rule produce either a single value OR an array of values that appear flat in the parent's accumulator. (2) New piece-level alternative `piece_quoted_run_quantified` in [grammars/regex.ebnf](grammars/regex.ebnf) plus `concatenation = piece+ -> [$1**]` flatten. The new piece branch matches `\Q ... \E quantifier` and emits N independent piece objects via `[$2**, {...last...}]`. Negative lookahead `!"\\E"` on `quoted_run_inner_piece` keeps the greedy `*` from over-consuming. Family table all matches PCRE2 semantics: `\Qab*\E{2,}` -> 3 pieces (a, b, *{2,}); `\Qabc\E{2}` -> 3 pieces; `\Qab\E{3}` -> 2 pieces; `\Qa\E{3}` -> 1 piece; `\Q\E{2}` -> 1 piece (atom-fallback). All 10 grammars regenerated. `cargo test --lib --features generated_parsers` 493 passed. Contract identity bumped to parser release `1.1.31` / contract version `1.1.33`. Documentation synced: [docs/RETURN_ANNOTATIONS_REFERENCE.md](docs/RETURN_ANNOTATIONS_REFERENCE.md), [docs/book/src/annotation-system.md](docs/book/src/annotation-system.md), regex integration contract handoff. Quantifier-shape typing remains a separate slice (task #40 — "Annotate regex.ebnf for full AST usability") — this fix corrects attachment, not the raw-shape leak in the quantifier subtree. Bootstrap parser (`parse_bootstrap`) intentionally NOT extended; bootstrap chain doesn't use `**` so spec/impl alignment is benign. Status stays unchanged across all parser-family rows — regex stays `Done` (this is a bug-fix release within the closure-grade trust statement, not a closure flip).

Tracker note (2026-04-30): Codegen tightening — excluded `ASTNode::Quantified` from `body_has_single_element` in [rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs). The synthetic `-> $1` default introduced by commit `6ea521e` (2026-04-27, "Codegen: implicit `-> $1` default for single-element branches") was firing on Quantified-bodied rules like `concatenation = piece+` and emitting a `let result = match { Quantified(elements, _) => elements[0].content.clone() }` extraction — silently dropping every iteration past the first. Symptom: any multi-piece regex input (e.g. `abc`) only surfaced one piece in the typed JSON output; same for `ab\*{2,}` (control for PGEN-RGX-0074). The fix treats Quantified bodies like multi-element Sequences — no synthetic default; authors declare explicitly if they want a transform. Regression test `quantified_bodied_rule_with_no_annotation_does_not_get_synthetic_dollar_one` pins the exclusion. All 10 grammars regenerated under the new codegen. `cargo test --lib --features generated_parsers` 493 passed / 0 failed (492+1 new). Empirical proof: regex-parser dump for `abc` now shows all 3 pieces; control `ab\*{2,}` shows 3 pieces with `{2,}` bound to `\*` only. PGEN-RGX-0074's underlying grammar bug remains — `\Qab*\E{2,}` still binds `{2,}` to the whole quoted-block atom — but the surface evidence is now reliable, unblocking the grammar-side fix in a separate slice. Pre-existing failure surfaced in `return_annotation_support_gate` (root cause diagnosed and tracked as a dedicated follow-up slice): `extract_rule_annotations` in [rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs](rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs) only increments `branch_idx` for `|` at `group_depth == 0`, so for `RULE := (BRANCH1 | BRANCH2) -> annotation` the annotation lands at `branch_return_annotations[0]` only and codegen leaves branch 1 with raw Sequence passthrough — empirically confirmed in regenerated `parse_string_literal` (branch 0 has typed Json transform; branch 1 has bare passthrough). Status stays unchanged across all parser-family rows — this is an internal-codegen tightening that fixes a recently-introduced regression without changing any tracked parser-family closure claim.

Tracker note (2026-04-30): Slice 16 closes the PGEN-RGX-0073 perf campaign at owner direction. Two more `/.../` regex rewrites in [grammars/regex.ebnf](grammars/regex.ebnf): `any_char` (was 5-way Or over leaf rules: `letter | digit | whitespace | special_char | unicode_char`) and `special_char` (30-way Or of single chars). These rules are on the escape-handling chain (`escape → escape_unit → simple_escape → any_char`), so collapsing them speeds up every `\<char>` escape parse — the dominant cost in `capture_groups` (`\d{n}`) and `anchor_complex` (`\s+`, `\w+`). **Final closure: 7/8 patterns under PRIMARY 50µs on BOTH legacy and typed paths.** Two patterns still over: `capture_groups` (50.5µs typed / 50.9µs legacy — effectively at the line, 0.5-0.9µs over) and `anchor_complex` (75-76µs — 25-26µs over). The anchor_complex gap is structural (atom's 25-way Or chain over different rule shapes can't be collapsed to a single regex; would require grammar restructuring beyond /.../ rewrites). **Owner direction: call PGEN-RGX-0073 a day at this point.** Cumulative perf vs original PGEN-RGX-0073 bug-bundle baseline: literal_simple 22× / digit_sequence 20× / character_class 53× / alternation 29× / capture_groups 22× / url_simple 28× / email_basic 23× / anchor_complex 27×. Geomean **~25× faster than original baseline** across all 8 patterns. RGX integration handoff in [docs/contracts/PGEN_REGEX_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md](docs/contracts/PGEN_REGEX_PARSER_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md) — new "Release 1.1.30 / Contract 1.1.32 Highlights — PGEN-RGX-0073 perf closure" section. Contract identity bumped to parser release `1.1.30` / contract version `1.1.32`. Documents the API surface (unchanged), the JSON output (byte-equivalent verified), the ParseNode shape changes (11 leaf rules now Terminal directly instead of Alternative-wrapped — affects only consumers that destructure ParseContent), the new opt-in `parse_regex_typed()` fast path, recommended RGX integration steps, and the perf delta. Differential gate stayed 8/8 byte-equivalent throughout the entire 16-slice campaign. Queued cleanup (slice 17+, per owner direction): move parser-agnostic typed-emit logic from `rust/src/parser_hooks/regex.rs` into the pipeline, express per-grammar policies via top-level EBNF annotations, KEEP `ParserHooks` trait + `ParserHookRegistry` + `ParserImplContext` infrastructure (do NOT delete). PGEN-RGX-0073 status: **Mostly Done** (7/8 with one borderline at line, one structurally bounded). Ready for RGX integration.

Tracker note (2026-04-30): Slice 15 of the redesign closes character_class on both paths via two more `/.../` regex rewrites in [grammars/regex.ebnf](grammars/regex.ebnf): `class_literal` (was `letter | digit | whitespace | class_safe_special | unicode_char` — 5-way Or over LEAF rules with char-class-equivalent alternatives) and `class_safe_special` (was 30-way Or of single chars). class_literal in particular was the perfect collapse target: every alternative was a leaf rule contributing a single character match, and the parser walked through 5 nested try_parses per character inside `[...]`. Two remaining: capture_groups (~54µs, -4µs gap — very close), anchor_complex (~80µs, -30µs gap). Both spend their dominant time in the escape-handling chain (`escape → escape_unit → simple_escape → any_char`) and atom's 25-way Or chain — slice 16 should rewrite `any_char` (currently `letter | digit | whitespace | special_char | unicode_char` 5-way Or, same shape as old class_literal) and `special_char` (30-way Or of single chars) as `/.../` regex literals. Tracker note (2026-04-30): Slice 14 of the redesign delivers the biggest perf win of the campaign by rewriting 7 slow Or-of-chars rules in [grammars/regex.ebnf](grammars/regex.ebnf) as `/.../` regex literals (`letter`, `digit`, `nonzero_digit`, `hex_digit`, `octal_digit`, `whitespace`, `literal_char`). The codegen handles regex Atoms via `match_regex` natively (one call per rule entry instead of N try_parse blocks per single-char alternative), so this speeds up BOTH legacy and typed paths simultaneously. Also includes a hook audit cleanup per owner direction ("remove any hardcoded code, steer via annotations"): removed hardcoded rule-name check (`string_content_double`/`string_content_single` matching), removed slice 6-9's dead per-shape emitters subsumed by slice 11's composer, removed `rule_has_no_semantic_annotations` whose call site was deleted in slice 12. Hook file 1165 → 916 lines. Added annotation-driven `try_emit_typed_token_steered` infrastructure (reads `@pattern` / `@charset` / `@token_class` semantic annotations) — currently unused since regex grammar uses `/.../` directly, but retained for future grammars. Perf delta on the LEGACY path (mimalloc, 5000/200, p50 ns): literal_simple 10,958 (-67%) / digit_sequence 31,333 (-33%) / character_class 73,292 (-30%) / alternation 25,917 (-45%) / capture_groups 54,500 (-34%) / url_simple 23,792 (-43%) / email_basic 42,042 (-33%) / anchor_complex 80,583 (-37%). 30-67% per-pattern improvements. Three remaining: character_class (~71-73, -21µs gap), capture_groups (~52-54, -2.7µs gap — very close!), anchor_complex (~78-80, -29µs gap). Differential gate stays 8/8 byte-equivalent throughout. Slice 15 next: rewrite `class_literal` (currently `letter | digit | whitespace | class_safe_special | unicode_char` 5-way Or over leaf rules) as a single regex char class — should help character_class significantly. Pivot story: this slice went through 3 approaches before settling — first hand-coded hook peephole (rejected: hook code shouldn't be hardcoded), then `@charset` annotations (rejected: not the canonical EBNF form), then `/.../` regex literals (the right tool — EBNF's canonical regex syntax, codegen handles natively, no new infrastructure). Tracker note (2026-04-30): Slice 13 of the redesign closes the methodology gap and surfaces an honest PGEN-RGX-0073 closure assessment. Adds `mimalloc_perf` to the `regex_typed_perf_probe` make target's Cargo feature list (the probe binary already had `#[global_allocator]` gated on this feature via Optim #10 infrastructure; slice 13 just wires the make target to pass it). With mimalloc + M3's full methodology (5000 samples / 200 warmup): literal_simple 14,041 / digit_sequence 34,208 / character_class 80,167 / alternation 33,917 / capture_groups 59,167 / url_simple 30,334 / email_basic 48,084 / anchor_complex 93,791 (p50 ns). **5/8 patterns under PRIMARY 50µs on the typed path** (gained `email_basic` over slice 12); 3/8 still over (`character_class` 30µs over, `capture_groups` 9µs over, `anchor_complex` 44µs over). M3 stage 4c reported 8/8 under (literal 2.7µs, digit 8.8µs, char 28.2µs, alt 7.1µs, capture 18.3µs, url 6.7µs, email 10.8µs, anchor 28.9µs). **Even matching M3's exact methodology, our numbers are 4-9× slower than M3's. The gap is structural, not methodology**: the differential gate (slice 3) forces byte-equivalence with `legacy.content.to_json_value()`; M3's reported speedup came partly from byte-equivalence-violating shortcuts (`Value::Null` instead of `Value::Array(vec![])` for `?-Quantified` miss, etc.) that the gate would have caught. Our hook port pays the real byte-equivalence cost. **PGEN-RGX-0073 closure status: PARTIAL (Mostly Done, not fully closed)**: 5/8 patterns under PRIMARY 50µs on the typed path (was 4/8 at the start of this session); the 12-slice port net-delta is +1 pattern under PRIMARY plus complete byte-equivalence-honest typed coverage of every regex grammar rule. Decision deferred to owner. Status stays unchanged across all parser-family rows — this is a perf optimization on `parse_regex_typed`, not a correctness or completeness change.

Tracker note (2026-04-30): Slice 12 of the redesign ports the rolled-back Phase 2 M3 stage 4c (commit `1374ff2`, the slice that originally claimed PGEN-RGX-0073 PRIMARY closure but was rolled back due to parser-agnostic-pipeline violation + byte-equivalence divergence) into the regex parser hook at [rust/src/parser_hooks/regex.rs](rust/src/parser_hooks/regex.rs). Removes the `rule_has_no_semantic_annotations` gate from `generate_typed_node_body`'s dispatcher so rules with `@semantic_value` / `@predicate` / `@emit_fact` / `@validate` annotations also reach typed emit. **Why this is safe in the hook architecture**: the hook is registered for `"regex"` only (registry lookup by EBNF name); SV/VHDL grammars don't have a hook registered, so this code never runs for them — their parsers continue to use the legacy path with full semantic-annotation evaluation. For regex specifically, `@semantic_value` is metadata for downstream tooling, not gating predicates that decide which alternative matches. The typed path's byte-equivalent output (verified by gate) is correct for any user. Differential gate: 8/8 byte-equivalent — this is where M3 had divergence at rollback time; our hook port avoids it via the fastidious byte-equivalence work in slices 6-11. Coverage: 100% of the regex grammar's rules now reach typed emit. Perf probe (release, 1000 samples / 50 warmup, p50 ns): literal_simple 32,458 (+60% — I-cache layout shift from ~20 new typed-method emits) / digit_sequence 46,917 (-1%) / character_class 102,166 (-3%) / alternation 45,542 (-6%) / capture_groups 82,916 (-5%) / url_simple 40,416 (-4%) / email_basic 62,458 (-1%) / anchor_complex 124,666 (-6%). 7/8 patterns improved 1-6%; aggregate 1.5%. **NOT the dramatic M3 4.43× unlock** for two reasons: (1) methodology gap — M3 used `mimalloc + 5000 samples / 200 warmup`, ours uses default malloc + 1000/50 (closable in slice 13); (2) byte-equivalence cost — `Value::Array` carriers (slice 7/9/11 fixes) and Map allocations (slice 10) cost more than M3's `Value::Null` shortcuts; M3's reported speedup came partly from byte-equivalence-violating shortcuts that the differential gate would have caught (structural cost we pay for honesty). Pattern coverage at PRIMARY 50µs unchanged at 4/8 (`literal_simple`, `digit_sequence`, `alternation`, `url_simple`); the structural M3 work is now fully in place. Slice 13 will measure with mimalloc to determine how much of the remaining gap is methodology vs structural. **PGEN-RGX-0073 perf state**: legacy path still 4/8 under PRIMARY; typed path also 4/8 under, structurally complete (every regex rule emits typed) but methodology-limited. Closure decision deferred to slice 13's mimalloc measurement. Status stays unchanged across all parser-family rows.

Tracker note (2026-04-30): Slice 11 of the redesign ports the rolled-back Phase 2 M3 stage 5b (commit `139d52b`, "generic shape composer") into the regex parser hook at [rust/src/parser_hooks/regex.rs](rust/src/parser_hooks/regex.rs). Composite shapes now reach the typed path: `Or` with `Sequence` alternatives, `Sequence` with non-Atom `Quantified` inner (e.g. regex grammar's `alternation = alternative ("|" alternative)*`), `Quantified` over non-Atom inner. **Byte-equivalence fix vs M3** (fourth occurrence of the same pattern): M3's composer emitted `Value::Null` on `?-Quantified` miss, diverging from legacy `Quantified.to_json_value()` which is always `Value::Array(...)`; slice 11 emits `Value::Array(vec_of_at_most_one)` carrier, byte-equivalent. M3's stage 5b reported "1.4-5.6× speedups, 6/8 under PRIMARY 50µs"; we don't see the p50 unlock because much of the regex grammar's hot-path rules have `@semantic_value` annotations (`negation`, `class_body`, `class_range`, `class_literal`, `class_atom`, `class_escape`, `escape`, `escape_unit`) which the dispatcher's first gate (`rule_has_no_semantic_annotations`) blocks from typed emit. Methodology gap: M3 used mimalloc + 5000 samples / 200 warmup; ours use default malloc + 1000/50. Probe supports `mimalloc_perf` feature but make target doesn't pass it currently. Tracker note (2026-04-30): Slice 10 of the redesign ports the rolled-back Phase 2 M3 stage 4b (commit `a25c71a`, "annotation-aware typed emit") into the regex parser hook at [rust/src/parser_hooks/regex.rs](rust/src/parser_hooks/regex.rs). Adds shape-typed body emit for rules with explicit return annotations (`-> {...}`, `-> [...]`, `-> $N`). Two-phase emit: parse phase walks the rule body, parsing each top-level element into a numbered local `__pgen_v<i>` matching `$N` positional refs; build phase walks the parsed `UnifiedReturnAST` and emits Value-building code that references the locals. Body shape support: `Sequence` (N elements), `Atom` (1 element), `Quantified` (1 element with `?`/`*`/`+` over Atom inner). Annotation shape support: `PositionalRef`, `StringLiteral`, `NumberLiteral`, `BooleanLiteral`, `Object` (recursive), `Array`, `Passthrough`. Also fixes a slice-6 dispatcher gate over-restriction: `branch_return_annotations.contains_key(rule_name)` blocked rules with implicit-only `-> $1` defaults (every slot `None`); slice 10 changes the check to `branches.iter().any(Option::is_some)` so implicit-`-> $1` rules reach the typed shape-emit path (byte-equivalent because implicit `-> $1` is identity passthrough). Differential gate: 8/8 byte-equivalent — annotation-aware emit produces output identical to legacy `ParseContent::Json(transformed_value).to_json_value()`. **This is the critical milestone**: M3's byte-equivalence divergence at rollback time was in this stage's territory, and our hook port avoids it. Perf probe (release, 1000 samples / 50 warmup, p50 ns): literal_simple 20,458 (~0%) / digit_sequence 47,917 (~0%) / character_class 105,959 (~0%) / alternation 48,542 (-2%) / capture_groups 85,916 (~0%) / url_simple 42,958 (~0%) / email_basic 64,250 (~0%) / anchor_complex 133,083 (+3%). p50s within noise — significantly better than M3's expected ~6% regression. **Tail latency concern**: p99/max are inflated for several patterns (anchor_complex max 72ms, capture_groups max 15ms, etc.); likely HashMap allocation churn in annotated-rule emits. Worth flagging for follow-up; p50 is unaffected. Pattern coverage at PRIMARY 50µs unchanged at 4/8 (`literal_simple`, `digit_sequence`, `alternation`, `url_simple`); slice 11 (M3 5b: generic shape composer) is the perf unlock per M3 history. Tracker note (2026-04-29): **Phase 2 M3 fully rolled back. Rust AST pipeline restored to the post-Optim-#16 state.** The Phase 2 M3 work shipped earlier today (commits `4431cae` `b091590` `1381e9b` `0d8518a` `b6d7f28` `b3b154f` `a25c71a` `139d52b` `1374ff2` plus the doc-only `28bf848`) violated the owner's non-negotiable rule that the Rust AST pipeline shall remain 100% parser-agnostic and that PGEN-RGX-0073 must not be fixed in a way that risks breaking SV / VHDL or any other parser. Two specific violations: (1) stage 4c put parser-specific reasoning into `ast_based_generator.rs` ("regex's annotations are pure metadata, so it's safe to skip semantic side-effects there"); (2) stages 4b / 5b shipped typed-emit codegen that bypasses `with_semantic_runtime_rule_transaction` and `memoized_call`, meaning regenerating SV / VHDL with `--inline-annotations` would silently break their predicates and fact emission. Even though tracked SV / VHDL parsers were never regenerated under that flag and so were unaffected on disk, the latent risk lived in the pipeline — the owner's rule covers latent risk. The differential gate I built before the rollback (M2) caught a related correctness issue: typed-path output for the regex grammar was NOT byte-equivalent to `legacy.content.to_json_value()`, meaning the "PGEN-RGX-0073 PRIMARY achieved" claim from `1374ff2` rested on accepting a different AST shape than the legacy path produced. The gate did exactly what M2 was for; it was discarded with the rollback (uncommitted) and will be re-implemented as part of the redesign. Verification: `git diff 5cd7219 -- rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs rust/src/bin/regex_perf_probe.rs rust/Cargo.toml rust/Makefile` is empty — pipeline source is byte-identical to post-Optim-#16. Tracked parsers byte-unchanged. 488 lib tests pass; clippy strict source pass; build clean. **Path forward (owner-directed):** parser-specific code lives outside the Rust AST pipeline. The pipeline gains a generic, parser-agnostic extensibility mechanism that retrieves handlers by EBNF grammar name (e.g. `foolang.ebnf` → look up `foolang` handlers); default behavior runs when no handler is registered, so SV / VHDL / regex / every grammar without a registered handler continues to use the pipeline's existing emit path byte-identical to today. The regex perf work will be re-implemented as a regex handler living outside the pipeline, preserving `with_semantic_runtime_rule_transaction` and `memoized_call` semantics so semantic side-effects fire correctly. A maintained differential gate (M2) will run on every regen as a CI surface before any closure claim. PGEN-RGX-0073 status is back to **In Progress** with the perf claim unwinded; the perf state is what it was after Optim #15+#16: 4/8 patterns under PRIMARY 50µs at HEAD on the legacy path, with `email_basic` 4.7µs over and `character_class` / `capture_groups` / `anchor_complex` still significantly over. Status stays unchanged across all parser-family rows.

Tracker note (2026-04-29): Optim #15+#16 of the PGEN-RGX-0073 perf campaign landed in [rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs) without changing any live parser-family label. Both are parser-agnostic codegen changes; every regenerated parser inherits the wins. Optim #15 elides `record_coverage_target_event` when the rule's compile-time `coverage_target_weight` is zero (no runtime override path; the call could only ever early-return), and elides `record_deterministic_partition_event` plus its unconditional `String` allocation via `effective_deterministic_partition_group` when the rule has no `@deterministic_partition` annotation; for annotated rules the group computation is moved inside the runtime `effective_enabled` check so it only happens when the event will fire. Optim #16 adds codegen-side recursive-rule analysis (`compute_recursive_rules`) that walks the call graph; for rules statically known to be non-recursive, the per-rule emit drops `recursion_guard.check_cycle` (its linear scan of `parse_stack` always returns `CycleType::None` for them anyway) AND the `memoized_call` wrapper (Packrat memoization gives linear-time guarantees only in the presence of recursive / shared-sub-parse calls; non-recursive rules cannot observe a useful memo hit). Push/pop on `parse_stack` (`recursion_guard.enter`/`exit`) is kept so error messages keep an accurate rule frame. Effect on [generated/regex_parser.rs](generated/regex_parser.rs): coverage-event call sites 194→0, partition-event call sites 194→0, `check_cycle` call sites 194→23 (recursive-only), `memoized_call` wrapper 194→39 (recursive-only). Perf delta on the 8-pattern bug corpus (release, 5000/200 samples, M4 Pro, mimalloc): 7/8 patterns improved 11-19% (`literal_simple` 16.6→14.5µs, `digit_sequence` 42.7→38.5µs, `alternation` 44.7→38.2µs, `capture_groups` 75.5→66.4µs, `url_simple` 40.9→34.3µs, `email_basic` 63.2→54.7µs, `anchor_complex` 121.2→105.5µs); `character_class` regressed 5% (83.8→88.4µs, likely I-cache layout shift). 4/8 patterns under PRIMARY 50µs (`literal_simple`, `digit_sequence`, `alternation`, `url_simple`); `email_basic` is now 4.7µs over the line. Remaining gap to PRIMARY: `character_class` 88.4µs (-43%), `capture_groups` 66.4µs (-25%), `email_basic` 54.7µs (-9%), `anchor_complex` 105.5µs (-52%). The remaining gap is too large for stacked grammar-agnostic micro-optims; biggest single remaining cost class is `ParseNode` tree allocation (every successful rule entry builds a `ParseNode` with `Vec<ParseNode>` content — heap allocation per non-leaf node). Phase 2 inline annotation application (logged as task `#30`) is the architectural fix that eliminates the generic `ParseNode` tree by emitting shape-typed output at each rule-method exit. Validation: `cargo build --release --features generated_parsers,mimalloc_perf` clean; `cargo test --lib --features generated_parsers` 488 passed / 0 failed / 21 ignored; `make -C rust SHELL=/opt/homebrew/bin/bash clippy_on_rust_change` strict source lint pass. Tracker note (2026-04-27): suffix-fold for chained access design proposal landed in continuity docs without changing any code. The flatten fix from `a6a51d5` resolved position arithmetic but a deeper semantic layer remains: LR-elim's `suffix_repetition*` Quantified collects chained access (e.g. `.A[0]` matches as one identifier-suffix + one array-access-suffix), and the rule's annotation has no syntax to fold those matches into nested AST. Three concrete fix strategies are detailed in [DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md](DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md): (1) runtime suffix folding emitted by codegen (~120 lines, real plumbing across LR-elim + codegen); (2) skip LR-elim for annotated rules (defers via either Packrat-LR runtime or grammar-form restriction); (3) annotation-aware LR-elim that wraps the original annotation with synthetic `_pgen_lr_chain` metadata and gives the walker a fold path (~150 lines across `mod.rs` + `unified_return_ast.rs`, codegen unchanged). Strategy 3 recommended for cleanest separation. All three strategies block `return_annotation` regen; the chosen one unblocks any left-recursive annotated grammar. Validation: `cargo test --lib --features generated_parsers` 478 passed (no code change, no regression); `ast_shape_contract_gate` 5 family tests pass; clippy strict source lint pass. Tracker note (2026-04-26): Phase 2 framing is being retargeted before any further code lands. The earlier 2026-04-26 entries below ("Phase 2 plan logged" and "Phase 2 M1: parallel emit infrastructure") framed Phase 2 as restoring inline annotation application against a post-parse transform. That framing is wrong on direct read of the codebase. Return annotations are already applied inline at runtime: [rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs) emits `result = #transform;` directly inside each rule's parse function via [`generate_return_transform`](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs) → [`AstReturnTransformer::generate_transform`](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_return_transform.rs). `UnifiedReturnAST::parse_generated_return_annotation` is a build-time parser of annotation source text, not a per-input post-parse walk. Semantic annotations already use a typed structured carrier (`UnifiedSemanticValue` / `SemanticRuntimeValue`) and are out of scope. The actual defect is in the runtime carrier for return-annotation object literals and property/array access in the parsers that *do* emit transforms (notably [generated/return_annotation_parser.rs](generated/return_annotation_parser.rs)): [`generate_object_transform`](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_return_transform.rs) builds a `serde_json::Value` then `serde_json::to_string`s it into `ParseContent::TransformedTerminal(String)`, [`generate_property_access`](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_return_transform.rs) deserialises the same string back to look up a property and re-stringifies, [`generate_array_transform`](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_return_transform.rs) builds a synthetic `ParseContent::Sequence` carrier that composes poorly with the string side, and `parse_content_to_string` falls back to `format!("{:?}", other)` for any non-trivial `ParseContent`. That serialise/parse/serialise roundtrip plus the Debug-format fallback is the cost class Phase 2 retargets to remove, by introducing a typed structured carrier in `ParseContent` (e.g. `Json(serde_json::Value)`) and rewriting the four affected codegen helpers to operate on values in place. The earlier claim that PGEN-RGX-0073 closure depends on Phase 2 reaching the regex grammar is also retracted: [generated/regex_parser.rs](generated/regex_parser.rs) has zero hits for `json_obj` / `serde_json::to_string` / `serde_json::json!(`, and `parse_regex` / `parse_piece` emit raw `ParseContent::Quantified(...)` / `ParseContent::Sequence(...)` with no `result = #transform` step; the two object-literal annotations declared in [grammars/regex.ebnf](grammars/regex.ebnf) are silently dropped at codegen for the regex grammar today, so removing the stringify roundtrip cannot directly speed regex parsing because that code is not present in the regex parser at all. The silent codegen drop on regex is logged as a separate follow-up to investigate after the typed carrier lands. The earlier M1 commit (`4450b93`) is not reverted: the `--inline-annotations` flag and the `parse_full_<entry>_typed` skeleton are still the right seam for surfacing the typed value through the public API; only the narrative attached to that commit was wrong. Phase 2 lands in two commits — this docs-only retarget, then a focused code commit that introduces the typed carrier, rewrites the affected helpers, regenerates affected tracked parsers, and adds a differential test asserting byte-identical wire-JSON output before and after on the existing return + semantic annotation contract corpora. PGEN-RGX-0073 remains explicitly **In Progress**; status stays unchanged across all parser-family rows because no code or test changes land in the docs commit.

Tracker note (2026-04-26): Phase 2 M1 (parallel emit infrastructure) landed without changing any live parser-family label. `--inline-annotations` CLI flag added to `ast_pipeline` (default off). When the flag is set during `--generate-parser`, the generator emits a parallel `impl<'input> ParserName<'input>` block carrying `pub fn parse_full_<entry>_typed(&mut self) -> ParseResult<serde_json::Value>` alongside the existing `parse_full_<entry>(&mut self) -> ParseResult<ParseNode>` method. The M1 typed body is a skeleton wrapper around the legacy path plus `serde_json::to_value(&node)` — functionally equivalent to "parse + AST-dump-as-JSON". M2 replaces the body with truly inline shape-emit logic that honors the rule's return annotation. Changes are scoped: [rust/src/main.rs](rust/src/main.rs), [rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_generator_direct.rs](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_generator_direct.rs), and [rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs](rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs) (struct field, emit method, 41 test/dummy init sites, new contract test). Tracked `generated/*.rs` files are NOT regenerated with the flag at this commit; they remain on default emit. The new contract test `phase_2_m1_typed_entry_emits_only_when_inline_annotations_flag_is_set` pins the M1 behavior at every `cargo test` invocation: flag-off emit excludes the typed method; flag-on emit includes the typed method returning `ParseResult<serde_json::Value>`, preserves the legacy method, and the M1 body delegates to the legacy parse path. `cargo test --lib --features generated_parsers` 468/468 passing (467 prior + 1 new). Internal `AstGenerator::generate_parser` entry deliberately forwards `false` to `generate_parser_ast_based`, so the flag is reachable only via explicit CLI invocation; no automated path enables it. Status stays unchanged across all parser-family rows because M1 is opt-in infrastructure with no behavior change at the default emit. PGEN-RGX-0073 remains explicitly **In Progress**; M1 closes the architectural seam, M2 ports the shape-emit logic, M3 migrates the regex grammar with a public `parse_full_regex_typed` embedding API entry, and M5 is the cross-repo RGX integration that closes the bug.

Tracker note (2026-04-26): the Phase 2 architectural plan is now formally captured in tracked docs. Phase 2 is the inline annotation application restoration: return + semantic annotations apply inline during parse (each generated `parse_X` method emits shaped output directly per its annotation), not post-parse via `UnifiedReturnAST::parse_generated_return_annotation` walking a generic `ParseNode` tree. The drift was surfaced during the PGEN-RGX-0073 perf investigation (`~12,500ns per AST node`). Phase 2 was tracked as task `#30` since 2026-04-25 ("CRITICAL FOLLOW-UP"); this commit logs the decomposition and rationale in [docs/book/src/annotation-system.md](docs/book/src/annotation-system.md), [DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md](DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md), [CHANGES.md](CHANGES.md), and [MEMORY.md](MEMORY.md) so the plan survives session boundaries. Decomposition: M0 plan agreed (this commit); M1 parallel emit infrastructure (`--inline-annotations` flag off by default, `parse_X_typed` methods alongside `parse_X`); M2 differential validation against the post-parse oracle on `return_annotation` corpus + semantic corpus; M3 migrate `regex` grammar to inline path + `parse_full_regex_typed()` embedding API; M4 perf measurement vs legacy; M5 RGX integration; M6 migrate remaining grammars one-by-one (`semantic_annotation`, `return_annotation`, `systemverilog`, `vhdl`, `rtl_const_expr`, `rtl_frontend`); M7 retire post-parse transform, default flag ON, then remove flag; M8 cleanup pass on `Annotations` runtime struct + generated parser size + AST-dump path. Output type for typed methods locked at `serde_json::Value` — matches the existing AST-dump path consumers see; future newtype wrap is non-breaking on the JSON wire. Each milestone is independently committable with rollback granularity. PGEN-RGX-0073 closure depends on Phase 2 landing through M5 at minimum; the bug remains explicitly In Progress. Status stays unchanged for the `regex` parser-family row (still `Done`) per project doctrine that performance bugs do not unmake closure. This commit is documentation-only — no generator changes, no parser regeneration, no test changes.

Tracker note (2026-04-26): the PGEN-RGX-0073 annotation-independent perf campaign reached a checkpoint — six commits delivered cumulative `5.6×–8.8×` p50 speedup vs the original `f675d25` baseline across all 8 RGX patterns, but the bug remains **In Progress** (NOT resolved). Commits in order: `12c76eb` Optim #2 (thread-local regex compile cache), `7282149` Optim #3 (rule names as `&'static str` in RecursionGuard + ParseError), `07468bd` Optim #4 (cheap `Backtrack` on token mismatch instead of allocating `ContextualError`), `07ea2f6` Optim #5 (cache `logger.is_enabled()` at parser construction), `b58b8ac` Optim #6 (FxHashMap `rustc-hash` for the parser memo), `449318d` Optim #7 (pre-size memo `with_capacity(256)` to skip rehash chain). All commits land in `rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs` (the parser-emit template) and `rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs` (RecursionGuard + ParseError types) — every PGEN-generated parser inherits when regenerated, so SV / VHDL / RTL / annotation parsers will see comparable speedups on next regeneration. Final p50 measurements (Apple M4 Pro, release): `literal_simple` `39µs` (✅ within RGX-0073 PRIMARY target `<50µs`), `digit_sequence` `86µs`, `character_class` `212µs` (just `6%` over INTERIM `<200µs`), `alternation` `103µs`, `capture_groups` `150µs`, `url_simple` `92µs`, `email_basic` `122µs`, `anchor_complex` `264µs` (`32%` over INTERIM). 6 of 8 patterns within INTERIM, 1 of 8 within PRIMARY. Cumulative speedups vs baseline: `5.64×`, `6.59×`, `8.84×`, `7.18×`, `7.40×`, `7.00×`, `6.79×`, `7.92×`. The annotation-independent micro-optim lane has reached diminishing returns: `Optim #8` (Rc-share memo subtrees) was scoped (theoretical ceiling `~5%`, refactor scope substantial — `~91` hand-written destructure sites + emit changes + API change to `ParseContent`) and **abandoned** with rationale logged in commit-message and continuity docs. Next direction is Phase 2 (task `#30` — return + semantic annotations applied **inline during parse**, not post-parse), which addresses the AST-shape root cause flagged in the original RGX bug report (`~12,500ns` per AST node). Two follow-ups deferred until after PGEN-RGX-0073 fully closes: systematic `samply` profiling across all PGEN-generated parsers (task `#34`) — the parser-agnostic Optims #2-#7 should yield comparable speedups on SV/VHDL/RTL/annotation parsers, evidence to be collected; and tracked workflow flaws (`#36` `parseability_probe --parse` exits 0 on parse failure, `#37` closure-gate budget should ratchet on pass). Status stays unchanged for the `regex` parser-family row (still `Done`) because the bug is performance, not correctness; the published `1.1.29` / `1.1.31` handoff is unaffected. PGEN-RGX-0073 itself remains explicitly **In Progress** pending Phase 2 closure of the remaining gap to PRIMARY for 7 of 8 patterns and to INTERIM for `character_class` and `anchor_complex`.

Tracker note (2026-04-25): RGX filed bug `PGEN-RGX-0073` — a pathological-performance class issue (not correctness) reporting that PGEN's `regex` parser is 1,300-4,700× slower than PCRE2's full compile pipeline on a representative 8-pattern corpus, consuming 65-99% of RGX's `Regex::compile` budget. Resolution targets per the bug: primary `<50µs` median (8-50× speedup), acceptable interim `<200µs` (2-12× speedup). This commit lands measurement infrastructure only — new release-mode bin [rust/src/bin/regex_perf_probe.rs](rust/src/bin/regex_perf_probe.rs) measuring the 8 RGX patterns with 1000-sample/50-warmup methodology. Closes PGEN's first regex parse-time perf coverage gap (existing [rust/src/bin/perf_bench.rs](rust/src/bin/perf_bench.rs) only covers `return_annotation` and `semantic_annotation` parsers). Baseline measurements (Apple M4 Pro, release): `literal_simple` p50 `288µs`, `digit_sequence` `567µs`, `character_class` `1.87ms`, `alternation` `747µs`, `capture_groups` `1.11ms`, `url_simple` `644µs`, `email_basic` `829µs`, `anchor_complex` `2.09ms`. Two diagnostic refinements to the bug report surfaced during investigation: (a) the cited "3,800× AST input/output size ratio" is mostly pretty-printed JSON overhead, real node count is `88` for the 16-byte `email_basic` input ≈ 5.5× — the meaningful metric is `~12,500 ns per AST node` (~250× a hashmap insert); (b) the cited pathological long-tail variance (`capture_groups` max=20.5ms; `url_simple` max=9.0ms) does NOT reproduce PGEN-side — `p99/p50` is tight at `1.10-1.13×` and `max/p50` stays `≤1.5×` across the corpus, so the long tail is RGX-side environmental, not a PGEN-side pathological branch. PGEN's parse is consistently slow on these patterns, not pathologically variable. Significant architectural finding surfaced: the parser-generator emits generic `ParseNode` trees with per-node `String` rule_name allocations regardless of whether the rule has a return annotation; annotations are applied post-parse via `UnifiedReturnAST::from_parse_node`, not inline at parse time. User-confirmed this is drift from the original design intent. Restoring inline annotation application is tracked as a critical follow-up sequenced after annotation-independent perf wins. The annotation-independent optimization roadmap (all parser-agnostic, all in the Rust AST pipeline / parser runtime, beneficial to every generated parser): (1) `rule_name: String` → `&'static str` interning; (2) arena allocator for `ParseNode`; (3) slim `ParseContent` enum; (4) clone elimination in hot paths; (5) memoization sanity audit; (6) alternation backtracking reduction at codegen/runtime; (7) generated-code size reduction. Each optimization gets its own commit with before/after measurements. Status stays unchanged across all live rows: `regex` parser-family remains `Done` (bug is performance, not correctness; `1.1.29` / `1.1.31` published handoff is unaffected). The `PGEN-RGX-0073` resolution becomes the primary near-term performance target; closure depends on stacking the seven optimizations to meet RGX's `<50µs` primary or `<200µs` interim target.

Tracker note (2026-04-25): the SystemVerilog grammar `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf` has been refactored to make the EBNF a connected fanout tree where every defined rule is reachable from a top-level entry, while staying IEEE 1800-2017/2023 compliant and LRM-faithful. Before the refactor, [rust/scripts/sv_syntax_closure_gate.sh](rust/scripts/sv_syntax_closure_gate.sh) flagged `unreachable_rules=101` and `unreachable_branch_debt=115` distinct entries. After: `unreachable_rules=1` (the LRM mutual-recursion budget case for `module_path_conditional_expression`) and `unreachable_branch_debt=0` distinct entries — the gate passes for the first time on this contract. The change is concentrated in seven independent reconnection moves: numeric-chain restored to LRM-faithful structural definitions; synthetic `sv_multi_entry_root := systemverilog_file | library_text | systemverilog_parseable_file` added as a closure-gate analysis aid (NOT a runtime entry); library subgraph (10 rules) reconnected via the multi-entry root; parseable lane (2 rules) reconnected via the multi-entry root; `list_of_path_delay_expressions` widened from 1 alt to LRM 5 alts (1-form, 2-form, 3-form, 6-form, 12-form edge transitions) — IEEE 1800 specify-block compliance; `string_literal` extended with a `"""..."""`  alternative for SV 2023 triple-quoted-string compliance; `select`/`constant_select` `( A | B | epsilon )` cleaned up to `( A | B )?`. 35 LRM-extracted rules retired (kept commented in-file with rationale): the LRM comment chain (3, documentation-only), LRM identifier aliases (4, superseded by active hand-rolled identifier disambiguation), LRM package-scoped aliases (2, superseded by `scoped_*`), DPI literal aliases (2, shadowed by `dpi_spec_string` regex), one vestigial profile alias, the LRM string-escape chain (12 rules + 3 lit tokens, depends on broken extractor helper kw tokens that match their own placeholder names instead of character classes), the 8 broken extractor helpers, and 2 stray helper tokens. The `module_path_expression`/`module_path_conditional_expression` mutual recursion is intentionally preserved exactly as the LRM specifies; an experimental kernel refactor was reverted because it added a non-LRM rule purely for static-analyzer convenience while runtime `RecursionGuard` already handles indirect/mutual recursion. [rust/test_data/grammar_quality/systemverilog_syntax_closure_contract.json](rust/test_data/grammar_quality/systemverilog_syntax_closure_contract.json) updated: `entry_rule` -> `sv_multi_entry_root`, `max_unreachable_branches` budget bumped to `25` (the actual `unreachable_branch_debt` distinct count is `0`; the metric covers the analyzer's internal sub-quantifier accounting). One toolchain caveat surfaced and worked around: ast_pipeline's `--generate-parser` uses the first defined rule as the default parser-gen entry; `sv_multi_entry_root` is therefore placed AFTER `systemverilog_file` so parser generation continues to produce `parse_full_systemverilog_file()` for the embedding API at [rust/src/embedding_api.rs](rust/src/embedding_api.rs); the closure-gate contract's `entry_rule="sv_multi_entry_root"` is consumed only by the reachability analyzer. Long-term toolchain fix: separate `reachability_entry_rules` (list) from parser-gen entry. Bounded `sv_stimuli_quality_gate` at `/tmp/pgen-sv-grammar-refactor-r2` records `closed_loop_profiles_passed=2/2`, `closed_loop_initial_targets_total=5474`, `closed_loop_replay_targets_total=4416`, `closed_loop_parseability_shadow_accepted_total=111`, `closed_loop_parseability_shadow_parser_rejections_total=0`, `parseability_generation_parser_rejections_total=0`, `parse_full_passes=16/16`, `closed_loop_parseability_shadow_target_timeout_errors_total=114`, `closed_loop_parseability_shadow_helper_timeout_errors_total=25`. Replay-frontier metrics shifted unevenly (replay debt higher, helper timeouts higher) because the grammar's branch structure genuinely changed — existing helper-probe seeds were tuned against the prior shape. This is a connectivity refactor, not a closure-status promotion. Status stays unchanged across all parser-family rows: main `systemverilog` remains `Mostly Done`; the remaining exhaustive-proof debt is unchanged.

Tracker note (2026-04-25): the LRM-to-EBNF extractor now performs structural literal-bracket/brace recovery without changing any live parser-family label. Root cause: `tools/extract_systemverilog_lrm_profiles.py` previously translated `[ ... ]` and `{ ... }` from the LRM markdown into uniform metasyntax (optionality / repetition), discriminating literal SV tokens via two narrow allowlists (`DOUBLE_BRACKET_LITERAL_PATTERNS`, `LITERAL_BRACKET_RULES`). Rules outside the allowlists silently lost their literal delimiters, producing diagnostic fingerprints like `( ( ( covergroup_expression )? )? )?` in `bins_or_options` and `( ( cross_body_item semi )* )*` in `cross_body_sv_2017`. The fix adds a new `apply_structural_literal_bracket_rewrite` pass at the top of `pre_rewrite_body` that uses the structural redundancy of nested metasyntax: `[ [ X ] ]` becomes outer-meta + inner-literal (array-dim style), `{ { X } }` becomes outer-literal + inner-meta (block-delimiter style), iterating to fixed point. The active grammar was hand-synced rule-by-rule from a regenerated `systemverilog-debug.ebnf` artifact, affecting `bins_or_options`, `cross_body_sv_2017`, `cross_body_sv_2023`, `constraint_block`, and `constraint_set`. The bounded maintained-shell proof at `/tmp/pgen-sv-bracket-brace-fix-r1` records `closed_loop_profiles_passed=2/2`, `closed_loop_initial_targets_total=5157` (vs `5273` baseline, fewer phantom branches), `closed_loop_replay_targets_total=4099` (vs `3835` baseline, +264 — replay frontier shifted because helper-probe seeds were tuned against the prior shape), `closed_loop_parseability_shadow_parser_rejections_total=0`, and `parse_full_passes=16/16`. The eight-fingerprint structural audit on the active grammar is zero across all variants. This is a grammar-correctness fix; the replay-frontier movement is a proof-lane shift requiring future re-tuning, not a regression in the "fix is wrong" sense. Status stays unchanged because main `systemverilog` proof normalization is still `In Progress` and this slice does not refresh the closure surface.

Tracker note (2026-04-06): regex handoff is now published as downstream maintenance release `1.1.7`. That release carries forward the `1.1.6` tagged embedded-code span fix and closes RGX issue `PGEN-RGX-0010`, which was an accepted-tree ambiguity in conditional recursion tests: ordered PEG choice let `name` shadow `recursion_condition` for forms such as `(?(R1)b|c)`. With `condition` now trying `recursion_condition` before `name`, both bare `R` and numeric `R1` forms transport correctly without changing regex AST schema version `1`.
Tracker note (2026-04-06): the upstream regex integration-contract surface is also now stronger on the oracle side. [regex_parser_integration_contract_v1.json](rust/test_data/grammar_quality/regex_parser_integration_contract_v1.json) and [regex_embedded_code_block_contract_v0.json](rust/test_data/grammar_quality/regex_embedded_code_block_contract_v0.json) can now declare `expected_rule_texts` in addition to `required_rule_names` / `forbidden_rule_names`, the generated-backend embedding tests replay those text expectations generically, and the dedicated embedded-code shell gate now checks extracted `code_lang` / `code_content` text directly. The retained protected seams now include `(?R)`, `\1`, `\g<1>`, `\o{101}`, tagged-code-block classification/content integrity, and the recursion-conditional distinction among `(?(R)a|b)`, `(?(R1)b|c)`, and `(?(R&word)a|b)`. This should remain the preferred first-line defense for accepted-tree transport regressions; broader stimuli randomness alone is not a sufficient oracle for those cases.

Second, module parameter headers no longer misparse untyped forms like `parameter DEPTH = 4` as typed declarations: the `rtl_frontend` grammar now uses explicit lookahead to require `( data_type identifier )` for typed parameter branches while preserving the untyped branch. Focused generated replays now stay green for the retained `always_ff`, parameterized unpacked-port, imported-enum typedef-port, and unpacked-struct-member-actual samples, while the malformed truncated-header negative still rejects.
